text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

text:
Before using Flonase Nasal Spray, tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or cataracts.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease.
Tell your doctor if you have diabetes.
Tell your doctor if you have herpes simplex virus of your eyes.
Tell your doctor if you have tuberculosis or any other infection.
Tell your doctor if you have sores or ulcers inside your nose.
Tell your doctor if you have recently had injury of or surgery on your nose.
You may start to feel relief on the first day.
Flonase can take several days of regular once-daily use before you get the full effect.
Tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve within 7 days.
Tell your doctor if you develop new symptoms such as severe facial pain or thick nasal discharge.
Corticosteroids can affect the way your immune system responds to infection.
Avoid being near people who are sick or have infections.
Stop use and ask a doctor if you have, or come into contact with someone who has, chickenpox, measles, or tuberculosis.
Do not administer Flonase Allergy Relief Nasal Spray to a child younger than 4 years old.

section_heading: How should I use Flonase Nasal Spray?
text:
Use Flonase exactly as directed on the label, or as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Do not share this medicine with another person, even if person have the same symptoms you have.
Sharing a bottle can spread germs.
Your dose will depend on the fluticasone brand or strength you use.
Your dose may change once your symptoms improve.
Follow all dosing instructions very carefully.
A child using the nasal spray should be supervised by an adult.
Read and carefully follow any Instructions for Use provided with your medicine.
Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you do not understand these instructions.
Shake the bottle before each use.
Flonase Allergy Relief should be shaken gently.
Flonase Sensimist should be shaken vigorously.
Use this product only once a day and do not use more than directed.
Avoid getting the spray in your eyes or mouth.
If you switched to fluticasone from another steroid medicine, you should not stop using steroid medicine suddenly.

section_heading: How should I use Flonase Nasal Spray?
text:
Follow your doctor's instructions about tapering your dose.
Storage differs between products.
Store Flonase Allergy Relief and Children's Flonase Allergy Relief between 4°C and 30°C (39°F and 86°F).
Store Flonase Sensimist between 15°C and 30°C (59°F and 86°F), and do not refrigerate or freeze Flonase Sensimist.
Throw the bottle away once you have used the number of sprays stated on the carton, even if there is still liquid in the bottle.
The correct amount of medicine in each spray cannot be assured after the labeled number of sprays has been used.
Bottle sizes vary between products and pack sizes.
They range from 30 to 144 metered sprays.
Dosing information:
Usual Adult Dose for Rhinitis (adults and children 12 years of age and older):
Flonase Allergy Relief Nasal Spray (fluticasone propionate 50 mcg per spray):
Week 1: use 2 sprays in each nostril once daily
Week 2 through 6 months: use 1 or 2 sprays in each nostril once daily, as needed to treat your symptoms
After 6 months of daily use: ask your doctor if you can keep using this medicine

Week 1: use 2 sprays in each nostril once daily
Week 2 through 6 months: use 1 or 2 sprays in each nostril once daily, as needed to treat your symptoms
After 6 months of daily use: ask your doctor if you can keep using Flonase Sensimist Nasal Spray
Usual Pediatric Dose for Rhinitis:
The recommended age group is 4 to 11 years.
The medication is Flonase Allergy Relief or Children's Flonase Allergy Relief (fluticasone propionate 50 mcg per spray).
The dosage is 1 spray in each nostril once daily.
2 to 11 years: Flonase Sensimist or Children's Flonase Sensimist (fluticasone furoate 27.5 mcg per spray): 1 spray in each nostril once daily.
Under 4 years: do not use fluticasone propionate nasal spray.
Under 2 years: do not use fluticasone furoate nasal spray.
An adult should supervise a child using the spray.
Children should use it for the shortest amount of time necessary to achieve symptom relief.
Talk to your child's doctor if your child needs to use the spray for longer than two months a year.

section_heading: How should I use Flonase Nasal Spray?
text:
What happens if I miss a dose?
:
Use the medicine as soon as you can.
Skip the missed dose if it is almost time for your next dose.
Do not use two doses at one time.
What happens if I overdose?
:
Seek emergency medical attention or call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222.
An overdose of Flonase is not expected to produce life-threatening symptoms.
Using more than the recommended dose may increase the chance of corticosteroid-related side effects.
Using Flonase for longer than directed may increase the chance of corticosteroid-related side effects.
These side effects include cataracts or glaucoma.
These side effects include adrenal gland problems.
These side effects include an increased risk of infection.
These side effects include sores inside the nose.
These side effects include slower growth in children.

section_heading: What other drugs will affect Flonase?
text:
Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all your other medicines, especially:
an antifungal medicine, such as ketoconazole tablets;
an antiviral medicine to treat hepatitis C or HIV/AIDS, such as ritonavir; or
another steroid medicine for asthma, allergies or skin rash.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with fluticasone nasal.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.
